When a join key passes the gate (rows_per_use = table_rows / n_distinct is small), rank it among the top candidates: prefer the key with the highest join_query_count, then the largest table_rows. Do not drop a join key merely because another candidate has a smaller rows_per_use.
6. Conviction over coverage: return the fewest candidates that cover the workload's dominant selective access paths. Every extra name must be justified by clearly better lookup selectivity or clearly wider selective reach; do NOT spend storage on weak indexes -- an index that barely helps still consumes budget and can leave the whole workload no better off.
7. Prefer indexes that sit on large tables (see table_rows). Avoid indexing very small tables and columns with a very low ndv_ratio.
